To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people expect to perform at their current level, even if they have reason to believe that they have improved or that they will improve in the future.

(a) when people are improving, their judgments of learning are unaffected by their learning; (b) this bias cannot be explained by a lack of conscious belief that learning predicts future performance; (c) this bias cannot even be explained by the belief that current performance predicts future performance; and (d) this bias cannot explain the fact that people's estimates of past performance are accurate.

(a) judgments of future performance are biased in the same direction as judgments of past performance, (b) this performance bias is not eliminated by providing information about learning, (c) this bias is not eliminated even when participants believe that past learning predicts future performance, and (d) this bias is observed even when participants believe they have been learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: Why do people not expect to learn from experience?
the question of how learners judge their future performance.
the role that learning plays in judgments of learning and the role that judgments play in learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bias is not affected by the learning.
the bias in judgments of learning is due to the fact that learning is not observable and therefore not used to guide judgments of learning.
the performance bias is an artifact of the fact that learning is usually not observable, and when learning becomes observable, judgments of performance become guided by learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people do not use their own learning to predict their own learning.
judgments of learning are controlled by performance, not by learning.
people are not good at predicting their future performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people do not always use the same information for making judgments and decisions.
judgments are not always guided by what learners think they know, but by what they think others will observe them doing.
the performance bias is not an artifact of people's lack of awareness of their learning.
